problem:
A European put option is written on a stock.
Spot price S = 89.
Strike K = 98.
Time to expiry: 365 calendar days, so T = 365/365 years (ACT/365).
Risk-free rate r = 1.5% per year, continuously compounded.
The underlying pays no dividends (q = 0).
Volatility sigma = 22% per year.
Conventions: Volatility is annualised. Interest rate r and dividend yield q are annualised and continuously compounded. Time to expiry T is in years using ACT/365 (calendar days / 365). The underlying pays a continuous dividend yield q. European exercise (at expiry only). Black-Scholes-Merton model: the underlying follows geometric Brownian motion under the risk-neutral measure with constant r, q and sigma.
What is the fair value of the put today?
Give the option value in currency units as a single number. Answers within 0.00965 of the verified value are correct.
conventions: Volatility is annualised. Interest rate r and dividend yield q are annualised and continuously compounded. Time to expiry T is in years using ACT/365 (calendar days / 365). The underlying pays a continuous dividend yield q. European exercise (at expiry only). Black-Scholes-Merton model: the underlying follows geometric Brownian motion under the risk-neutral measure with constant r, q and sigma.

Spot price S = 118.
Strike K = 124.
Time to expiry: 91 calendar days, so T = 91/365 years (ACT/365).
Risk-free rate r = 4.25% per year, continuously compounded.
The underlying pays no dividends (q = 0).
Volatility sigma = 24% per year.
Barrier H = 94 (below the spot; not yet touched).
The down-and-out put is worth 6.788704.
Conventions: Volatility is annualised. Interest rate r and dividend yield q are annualised and continuously compounded. Time to expiry T is in years using ACT/365 (calendar days / 365). The underlying pays a continuous dividend yield q. European exercise (at expiry only). Black-Scholes-Merton model: the underlying follows geometric Brownian motion under the risk-neutral measure with constant r, q and sigma. The barrier is monitored continuously from today to expiry. Neither option pays a rebate. A knock-out option becomes worthless the first time the spot touches the barrier; a knock-in option becomes a vanilla option at that moment and otherwise expires worthless.
What is the value of the down-and-in put?
Give the option value in currency units as a single number. Answers within 0.0123 of the verified value are correct.
